description: This image displays three pie charts, each representing the distribution of four categories labeled N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K− across difficulty levels categorized as “easy,” “medium,” and “hard.” Each pie chart is segmented into four colored portions corresponding to these categories, with a shared legend indicating that teal represents N+K+, gold represents N−K+, orange represents N−K−, and red represents N+K−. The “medium” chart shows the largest segment as gold (N−K+) at 44.3%, followed by teal (N+K+) at 44.6%, then red (N+K−) at 7.2%, and the smallest segment as orange (N−K−) at 3.9%. The “hard” chart shows the largest segment as gold (N−K+) at 36.2%, followed by orange (N−K−) at 36.8%, then teal (N+K+) at 20.1%, and the smallest segment as red (N+K−) at 7.0%. All percentage values are labeled directly within their respective slices. The charts are arranged side-by-side with no visual emphasis such as exploded slices or bolded text.
